title: Negating Quantifiers and Null Quantification
quickIdea: Negation flips the quantifier: not for all becomes there exists not, and not there exists becomes for all not. A quantifier may slide past a subformula only when that subformula does not use its variable.
remember: not (for all x P(x)) is equivalent to there exists x (not P(x)).
not (there exists x P(x)) is equivalent to for all x (not P(x)).
Null quantification - W has no free x: for all x (P(x) or W) is equivalent to for all x P(x) or W, and there exists x (P(x) and W) is equivalent to there exists x P(x) and W.
Same restriction for and under the universal and or under the existential: the quantifier slides past W only because W does not mention x.
The arrow case is the trap: for all x (P(x) implies W) is NOT equivalent to (for all x P(x)) implies W. What is equivalent is there exists x (P(x) implies W).
Reason: P implies W is not P or W, and not (there exists x P(x)) is for all x (not P(x)).
Distribution: the universal distributes over and, the existential over or. Neither distributes over the other connective.

example.prompt: Negate: there exists x (for all y alpha(x, y) and for all z beta(x, z)).
example.work: not there exists becomes for all not; then De Morgan turns the and into an or of negations; then each negated universal becomes an existential with a negated body.
example.answer: For all x (there exists y not alpha(x, y) or there exists z not beta(x, z)).

gateAngle: GATE CS 2020 Q.39 asks which of four null-quantification laws is NOT valid, and the answer is the arrow one, for all x (p(x) implies W) versus (for all x p(x)) implies W. GATE CS 2013 Q.47 asks which formulas are not equivalent to a negated existential, and GATE awarded marks to all because two options were wrong.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: See GATE CS 2020 Q.39 and GATE CS 2013 Q.47 in the linked PYQs: one tests the arrow case, the other tests pushing a negation through two nested universals.
variations.answer: 2020: option (C) is not valid. 2013: options (A) and (D) are not equivalent.
variations.why: Both are decided by rewriting with not (for all x P) = there exists x (not P) and then applying propositional laws inside the scope.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: Simplify: not (there exists x for all y R(x, y)).
variations.answer: For all x there exists y (not R(x, y)).
variations.why: Each negation flips one quantifier and moves inward: not exists gives for all, and not for all gives exists.

trap.what: Assuming for all x (P(x) implies W) is the same as (for all x P(x)) implies W.
trap.why: The implication is a disjunction in disguise, and the negation that a disjunction carries moves the quantifier the other way.
trap.counterexample: Domain {1, 2}, P(1) true, P(2) false, W false. Left side: for all x (P(x) implies W) is (false) and (true implies false) - false. Right side: (for all x P(x)) implies W is false implies false - true. They differ.

check.question: Negate for all x there exists y R(x, y).
check.answer: There exists x for all y (not R(x, y)).
check.explanation: The negation flips both quantifiers in order and negates the body.
